title: Juniper switch (junos_exporter)
description: fksw and any other Junos device junos_exporter is pointed at. Provisioned by roles/junos_exporter -- edits made in the UI are overwritten on the next Ansible run.

panels.title: Temperature
panels.description: Routing-engine and CPU temperature. Separate panel from CPU utilisation on purpose -- percent and degrees do not share an axis.

panels.title: Errors and drops
panels.description: Flat zero is the expected reading. Anything sustained here is a cable, an optic or a duplex mismatch.

panels.title: Optical receive power
panels.description: Only populated for ports with a transceiver that reports diagnostics. A slow slide here is an optic going, usually weeks before the link drops.

panels.title: LLDP neighbours
panels.description: What the switch believes is plugged into each port. Handy for working out which physical box just went quiet.

panels.title: LACP member links
panels.description: ae1 and ae10-ae14. A member dropping to anything below Distributing halves the bundle without taking the aggregate down, so nothing else on this dashboard would show it.

panels.title: Virtual chassis
panels.description: Both preprovisioned members and the virtual-chassis ports between them.

panels.title: PoE power draw
panels.description: Per-port PoE consumption. Only ports actually delivering power report anything.

panels.title: FPC CPU
panels.description: Per-member CPU. On a virtual chassis this is the per-slot view that the routing-engine panels above do not give you.

panels.title: Filesystem used
panels.description: EX-class flash is small, and /var filling up is a classic way for one of these to start behaving strangely long before it actually falls over.
